title: Variational Learning of Disentangled Representations
claim: Data is generated from a condition-driven latent and an independent latent, which defines the structure the learning objective must match.
layout: Single panel, left-to-right graph, four circular nodes with arrows converging on x
description: A small probabilistic graphical model drawn with four circular nodes and black arrows on a white background. The observed variables y (top left) and x (right, middle) are filled light gray. The latent variables w (top middle) and z (bottom middle) are white. An arrow runs horizontally from y to w. From w, a line goes right and then turns down into x. From z, a line goes right and then turns up into x. The x node therefore receives two incoming arrows, one from w and one from z. The condition y influences only w, while z is independent of y. The eye goes first to the gray nodes and the converging arrows at x. There is no text beyond the variable symbols.
caption: Probabilistic graphical model: gray circles denote observed variables, white circles show latent variables.
abstract: Disentangled representations separate factors that are shared across conditions from those that are condition-specific. Such separation is needed for generalization to new domains, treatments, patients, or species. A dominant line of work pursues this goal through variational formulations. While these approaches achieve partial disentanglement, they often exhibit three common limitations: they either do not remove all condition-specific information from the condition-specific representation, allow the condition-specific representation to become uninformative, or impose independence assumptions that do not reflect the underlying generative process. In this work, we introduce DisCoVR, a variational framework that addresses these limitations. Its objective is aligned with the probabilistic structure of the data-generating process, and includes an adversarial term that prevents condition-specific information from being encoded in the condition-specific representation.DisCoVR reconstructs the data from both shared and condition-specific representations, ensuring that each remains informative, and uses a structured prior that further reinforces the informativeness of both representations. We show that across synthetic, image, and single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets, DisCoVR achieves stronger disentanglement compared to previous approaches.
